subject: CHEMISTRY
pageTitle: Ideal Gas Law (PV = nRT): Steps, Units and Examples
description: Solve gas problems with PV = nRT: pick R, convert to kelvin, and watch your units, with two worked chemistry examples.
caption: The ideal gas law in 7 swipes: when to use it, the kelvin rule, and two worked examples. Save this for your chemistry test. Free Chemistry study guide at precisstudy.com/chemistry (no sign-up).

slides.title: PV = nRT: THE GAS LAW THAT SOLVES EVERYTHING
THE EQUATION
slides.note: P in atm, V in liters, n in moles, T in kelvin.

slides.title: BEFORE YOU PLUG IN
slides.note: Temperature must be in kelvin every time.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: 0.50 mol of gas is in a 10. L container at 300 K. Find the pressure.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: What volume does 1.0 mol of gas occupy at 1.0 atm and 273 K?

slides.title: WATCH OUT
points: If pressure is in kPa or mmHg, convert it or use the matching R.
Volume must be in liters with R = 0.0821.
